value.body: An export-import executive keeps a company's cross-border shipments moving and its paperwork in order. Employers include exporters and importers, manufacturers that sell abroad, freight forwarders and customs brokers. A typical day involves preparing documents, booking and tracking shipments, and following up with buyers, banks and agents.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Com or BBA, often in International Business
items.note: Short export-import courses are a common add-on

items.label: Key documents
items.value: Invoice, packing list, shipping bill or bill of entry, bill of lading or airway bill, certificate of origin, letter of credit

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Customs and foreign-trade portals, Excel, ERP

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join as documentation or EXIM executives at exporters, freight forwarders or customs brokerage firms. Knowing Incoterms and the main shipping documents helps at interviews; an internship with a forwarder or exporter is a common way in.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Coordination with shippers, banks and agents

value.title: At a glance
items: Accuracy matters: document errors can hold up shipments or payments.
Work can follow other time zones and shipping cut-off times.
Next roles: EXIM manager, international sales, or a move into logistics or trade finance.

competition.note: B.Com graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education

women.note: Share of women among B.Com graduates in 2023-24 — the entry degree, not people already working in this role.
